facts.text: Mar Lin takes its name from Susan Marlin James, daughter of early settler John Marlin and grandmother of a U.S. congressman in Pennsylvania today.
Mar Lin grew during the late 19th and early 20th centuries as European immigrants—Poles, Lithuanians, Slovaks, Ukrainians, and others—moved to work in Schuylkill County’s anthracite mines.
Situated near Pottsville, the county seat, Mar Lin lies in the historic anthracite coal region of eastern Pennsylvania.
Mar Lin observes Eastern Time, shifting from standard UTC‑5 to daylight UTC‑4 between the second Sunday in March and the first Sunday in November.
Mar Lin is an unincorporated community within Norwegian Township, a rural area of Schuylkill County.
Mar Lin sits at 40°40′50″N 76°14′39″W, roughly 40.6805°N latitude and 76.2442°W longitude.
